pageTitle: Dong Lab | Cancer Research & Drug Discovery
description: The Dong Lab at the Vancouver Prostate Centre studies molecular biology and treatment resistance in cancer to guide the discovery of new therapeutic strategies.

hero.title: Understanding cancer.
hero.text: We study how cancer cells adapt to treatment—and how that knowledge can guide new therapeutic strategies.
hero.imageAlt: Conceptual illustration of molecular research and computer-aided drug discovery.

about.label: THE DONG LAB
about.title: From molecular questions to new possibilities.
about.text: Led by Dr. Xuesen Dong, our laboratory at the Vancouver Prostate Centre investigates the mechanisms that drive treatment resistance in prostate cancer. We bring together RNA biology, cancer research and computer-aided drug discovery to identify new ways to understand and target resistant disease.
about.affiliation: Vancouver Prostate Centre · Department of Urologic Sciences · The University of British Columbia

research.label: OUR RESEARCH
research.title: Three connected directions.
research.intro: Understanding cancer at the molecular level helps us ask better questions about detection and treatment.

areas.title: Cancer biology & treatment resistance
areas.text: We investigate how androgen receptor signalling, RNA-binding proteins and RNA regulation influence prostate cancer progression and adaptation to treatment.

areas.title: Biomarkers & disease insight
areas.text: We connect molecular pathology with RNA-based biomarker research, including circular RNAs, to understand prostate cancer and investigate signals of disease progression.

areas.title: Drug development
areas.text: We combine AI-enabled computer-aided drug design with experiments to discover and refine compounds targeting cancer-associated molecular processes.

approach.label: OUR APPROACH
approach.title: Discovery begins with a question.
approach.text: Why do tumours become resistant to treatment? Which molecular processes can we target? We investigate these questions by connecting computational analysis with laboratory experiments.
approach.imageAlt: Conceptual research illustration of a pipette, a culture dish and molecular structures.
